column3: The Hebrew uses the image of a mouth for the opening; BSB uses “opening.”
The Hebrew gives the wheel’s “height”; BSB calls it the diameter.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the corner supports “shoulders”; BSB uses “handles.”
The Hebrew says that the supports and panels were “from it”; BSB makes their being cast as a unit explicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses “right,” “left,” “eastward,” and “south”; BSB renders these as south, north, and the southeast corner. It says “house,” where BSB uses “temple.”
The Hebrew calls the first items “basins”; BSB uses “pots.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew places the bowls of the capitals on the front of the pillars; BSB places them atop the pillars.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says “one Sea”; BSB says “the Sea.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that the king cast them, using an active verb; BSB says that he had them cast.
The Hebrew says Solomon left the articles and that their weight was not investigated; BSB supplies “unweighed” and describes the weight as unable to be determined.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has singular “flower”; BSB uses plural “flowers.”
The Hebrew calls the building “house”; BSB uses “temple.”
Close to the Hebrew.
